# M10.1 — Physical memory discovery and read-only inventory

Date: 2026-11-25 (Asia/Kolkata)  
Result: **PASS**  
Baseline: `c1a4b07` on `main`, tag `v0.0.7-rc1`; `origin/main` pointed to the same commit when inspected. No commit, tag, or push was made.

## Objective and architecture

The kernel requests Limine base revision 6 memory map, HHDM offset, and executable address response through `.limine_requests`. It copies at most 256 validated half-open regions into static memory, rejects malformed maps, classifies the installed protocol's nine known types, and keeps unknown types unavailable. It performs no allocation or reclamation. The M09 descriptor activation and IF=0 remain intact. `CPUID.80000008H:EAX[7:0]` supplies the physical address width. A physical address identifies a location in the machine address space; a kernel pointer is a virtual address translated by page tables. HHDM supplies a mapping for eligible physical regions but is not a general way to translate arbitrary kernel pointers. Limine's executable address response plus its documented uniform executable mapping offset is used for image objects.

The protocol header used in the build is `external/limine-protocol/source/include/limine.h`. The [Limine protocol specification](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md) documents map types, the executable's uniform virtual to physical offset, and bootloader page tables living in bootloader-reclaimable memory. The [Intel SDM](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/874240/325462-090-sdm-vol-1-2abcd-3abcd-4.pdf) documents the CPUID physical width field and paging controls. The installed header governs the compiled field layouts and constants.

A usable region `[base,end)` contributes `max(0, floor(end/4096) - ceil(base/4096))` fully contained 4 KiB candidates. These are **not allocator-ready pages**: reservations are still preliminary. Total described bytes sum map entry lengths, including sparse firmware address ranges; this is not installed RAM.

## Validation and classification

The builder rejects missing responses, empty or oversized maps, null entries, zero length, address-width violation, wrapping endpoints or totals, unsorted entries, overlaps involving usable entries, and misaligned HHDM offsets. It permits unaligned region bounds and excludes partial pages. Known types 0–8 are usable, reserved, ACPI reclaimable, ACPI NVS, bad, bootloader reclaimable, kernel/modules, framebuffer, and reserved mapped. Other values enter a conservative unknown bucket. Bootloader, ACPI, firmware, framebuffer, and unknown regions remain unavailable. M10.2 corrected the overlap rule after checking the installed protocol: nonusable entries may overlap each other.

## Preliminary reservations

The 256 MiB KVM transcript reports the following exact or partial observations. The kernel image interval includes the ELF BSS memory size, not just file bytes. Executable image physical conversion uses the Limine executable-address response and uniform-offset guarantee. RSP establishes one current stack pointer only. CR3 establishes one physical root page only. Exact stack bounds, subordinate page-table pages, and Limine response backing remain unresolved and therefore reserved conservatively. The framebuffer's virtual address and memory-map category are reported; its dedicated mapping is not assumed to be ordinary RAM.

## Files and build

Created `kernel/memory_map.c`, `kernel/include/memory_map.h`, `experiments/m10-memory-inventory/main.c`, `experiments/m10-memory-inventory/limine.conf`, `experiments/m10-memory-inventory/linker.ld`, `scripts/build-m10-memory-inventory.sh`, `scripts/check-m10-memory-elf.py`, `scripts/test-m10-memory-inventory.py`, `scripts/test-m10-memory-host.sh`, and `tests/memory_map_test.c`. M09 source and linker behavior were left unchanged. The build uses freestanding GCC with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, GNU LD, and fixed ISO timestamps. The ELF audit checks request sections, entry and selected symbols/instructions. A scratch copy excluding `build`, `dist`, and `.git` produced byte-identical ELF and ISO.

The first freestanding build unexpectedly emitted compiler-generated `memset`/`memcpy`; `-fno-builtin` and explicit byte loops removed that dependency. The new host test initially had an overlapping fixture; correcting the fixture preserved the overlap-rejection check. The QEMU parser was updated to validate all regions and the new reservation transcript.

## Tests and evidence

- M09 baseline: **942/942 normal and 942/942 ASan/UBSan** checks through `scripts/test-rc1-host.sh`.
- M10 map tests at this artifact's build: **30/30 normal and 30/30 ASan/UBSan**. M10.2 adds two overlap checks, now **32/32** in both modes. LeakSanitizer disabled in the inherited sandbox runner; AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer ran.
- QEMU: **3/3 KVM** (256, 512, 1024 MiB) and **1/1 TCG** (256 MiB). Q35, one vCPU, fresh OVMF variables, ISO only. Runner independently recalculated all region lengths, categories, totals, page counts, and order.
- Each run reached `MEMORY INVENTORY: PASS`, preserved active GDT/IDT/TSS, and halted without reset. Monitor showed CPL=0, HLT=1, IF=0, and RIP `0xFFFFFFFF80002302` after the checkpoint HLT. Saved `monitor.txt`, `mappings.txt`, `kernel.log`, `emulator.log`, `screen.ppm`, and `result.json` in each run directory.
- Graphical capture: `build/m10-memory-inventory/run-fv_xs5f9/screen.png` (actual 1280×800 QEMU framebuffer). It shows the map count, usable bytes, and candidate pages.

## Limitations and M10.2

This is a read-only inventory. No pages have been allocated, freed, or reclaimed. The exact BSP stack allocation, Limine response backing, complete active page-table tree, and any firmware-owned subranges not separately exposed remain unresolved. M10.2 should construct an allocator-safe reservation set from all nonusable map entries, load-segment memory extents, mapped stack bounds, and a bounded reviewed page-table walk before enabling any physical allocator. It should then prove no candidate overlaps a reservation. Hardware interrupts remain disabled.

## Interview questions

1. **Why use half-open regions?** `[base,end)` makes length `end-base` and adjacent regions meet without overlap.
2. **What is HHDM?** A bootloader-created virtual mapping of eligible physical regions at a reported offset.
3. **Can HHDM convert any kernel pointer?** No. Kernel image and stack pointers can use other mappings.
4. **Why count fully contained pages?** A partly usable page may also contain reserved bytes.
5. **What does CPUID leaf 0x80000008 give?** The processor-supported physical-address width in EAX's low byte.
6. **Why leave bootloader-reclaimable memory untouched?** Live page tables and responses may still reside there.
7. **Why does total described exceed RAM?** The map includes sparse physical address ranges, including firmware MMIO reservations.
8. **Why include BSS in the kernel image?** Its zero-initialized data occupies memory even though it occupies no file payload.
9. **What does CR3 identify?** The physical root of the active page-table hierarchy, not every table page.
10. **Why is this inventory not an allocator?** It does not establish all occupied page bounds or manage ownership transitions.
